The repeated tread, edge line and riser pattern gives horizontal surfaces and vertical faces, so it reads as three-quarter. The 32-wide silhouette is uniform. Rows 32-47 are flat cave floor with no front face, which is normal for ground terrain.

Near-flat coverage is 27%, against 0% for both references. The sandy landing at the bottom is a large, almost untextured fill. surfaces.part: ground apron at foot of stairs

answer.evidence: Rows 0-31 show a repeating stair pattern. Each step has a tread band of 3-4 rows (rows 8-11, 17-20, 25-27) that ends in a 1-row light front-edge line (rows 12, 21, 28; also row 5 for the top step). Below each line are 2-3 rows of dark shadow or riser (rows 14-16, 22-24, 29-31). The steps therefore read as horizontal treads plus vertical risers, not a flat elevation. A dark vertical strip at x≈6-7 is the cliff wall edge, not an isometric side face. Rows 32-47 are flat ground at the foot of the stairs.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown stair face with horizontal step bars over a beige sandy base. Its outlines lean dark brown (only 19% of dark edge pixels are neutral), so they read as material tone, not a black sticker line. The shading is shallow, though. The stair wood has about 3-4 lightness steps and the base about 2-3, against the references' 5-6 per material. The whole piece uses only 11 distinct colours, and 27% of it is near-flat (exact 5x5 flat fill), mostly the beige base and the plain step risers. The references have 0% flat coverage. The measured 8 visible tones per tile beats the grass (3) and edges past the paving (7), but that comes from a few large contrasting bands, not from fine grain or per-stone detail. A careful artist would find it flatter and more graphic than the references, so I fail it.

Below each line, 2-4 rows of dark riser shadow (rows 13-16, 22-24, 30-31) form the front face. That is evidence (a) for a top surface plus a front face. A dark column on the left and a thin one on the right read as wall shading, not a receding side face. Rows 32-47 are a plain flat floor that continues the terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's dark edge pixels are only 19% neutral, so the outlines lean brown and count as dark material tone, which is good. Visible tones per tile (8) are above both references (3 and 7), so the density fact does not count against it. The weaknesses are structural. 27% near-flat coverage against 0% for both references means real flat fills: the sand strip at the bottom and the plain step faces are large uniform patches with little grain or speckle. The whole piece uses only 11 distinct colours. The stair treads and risers read as about 4 lightness steps, with simple horizontal bars and no per-plank grain or stone-by-stone shading.
